verdict.rationale: Mercury documents a broad API surface: transactions and categories, statements, cards (issue, set limits, lifecycle), invoices and customers, ACH/check/wire payouts, internal transfers, receipt attachments, webhooks, OAuth2 and scoped tokens. An official CLI, MCP server and Go SDK sit on top of it. However, Mercury never claims full UI parity, and some actions are documented as dashboard-only: gated disbursements require sign-off inside the Mercury dashboard, and access revocation is done from the dashboard. Missing for 10: explicit UI-parity commitment, API coverage of approvals/sign-off, user and permission management, reimbursements, bill pay, and account or credit applications, plus independent hands-on confirmation of parity.
